name: Gin Rummy
description: Gin Rummy is a two-player knock-rummy game where players draw and discard to build sets and runs, then end a hand by knocking with low deadwood or going gin with no deadwood.

overview.description: Gin Rummy is a two-player knock-rummy game where players draw and discard to build sets and runs, then end a hand by knocking with low deadwood or going gin with no deadwood.

history.origins: Gin Rummy was created by New York Bridge player Elwood T. Baker around 1911, from the Mexican game Conquian and the American game Rum.
timeline: Early 1910s: Developed in New York as a two-player rummy form.
1940s: Became a popular Hollywood and club game with bonus-heavy scoring variants.
Modern era: Remains a widely played competitive and casual two-player card game.
history.cultural: Gin Rummy became one of the best-known head-to-head card games in American social and tournament play.
history.evolution: Core draw-discard and knock structure remained stable while bonus values and deal procedures vary by table and tournament rules.

setup.players: Two players only, head-to-head; no partnerships. Each player receives ten cards per hand. Dealership alternates from round to round; the first dealer is often chosen by drawing cards from the pack (lower card deals), and subsequently the winner of the previous hand deals.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck, ace low in runs.
setup.dealing: Deal 10 cards to each player one at a time. Turn the next card face up as first discard and place the rest face down as stock.
setup.equipment: Scorepad for cumulative hand and game bonuses.

rules.objective: Win points by ending hands with lower deadwood than opponent and reach game target first.
rules.gameplay: On each turn draw one card from stock or top discard, then discard one card face up. If you took the top discard this turn, you cannot discard that same card immediately. Melds are sets (3-4 equal ranks) and runs (3+ same-suit consecutive cards); a card cannot count in two melds at once. Ace is always low, so A-2-3 is valid but A-K-Q is not. A player may knock after drawing if deadwood is 10 or less by discarding face down, then both hands are exposed. If knocker did not go gin, opponent may lay off unmatched cards on knocker melds. If stock reaches two cards and no one has knocked, hand is cancelled and redealt.
keyRules: First turn is special: non-dealer may take upcard; if declined, dealer may take it; if both decline, non-dealer draws stock.
Knock requires deadwood 10 or less; going gin means deadwood 0.
Opponent cannot lay off when knocker goes gin.
Cancelled hand (stock down to two cards without knock) scores no points and same dealer deals again.

strategy.basic: Lower deadwood early and avoid holding too many high cards that can punish you when opponent knocks.
strategy.intermediate: Use discard-pick information to infer opponent meld shapes and avoid feeding obvious runs or sets.
strategy.advanced: Balance knock timing against expected undercut risk by modeling opponent deadwood range from discard behavior.
tips: Cards taken from discard reveal information; take them mainly when immediate meld value is strong.
Watch stock depth because hands can end as cancellation when stock nears two cards.

variations.name: 25-Point Bonus Tables
variations.description: Some groups use 25 for gin bonus and/or undercut bonus instead of 20 and 10.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Bonus point overrides can be added to engine.constants when implementing this variant.

variations.name: Oklahoma Gin
variations.description: Initial upcard value sets knock limit and a spade upcard doubles hand score; game target is often 150.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Knock limit and target score overrides to be added from Oklahoma Gin rules.

variations.name: 11-Card Non-Dealer Start
variations.description: Alternative opening deals 11 to non-dealer and 10 to dealer with no upcard, then non-dealer discards first.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Deal pattern and first-actor overrides to be added when implementing this variant.

scoring.description: Hand scoring uses deadwood difference plus bonus events, and game scoring continues across hands.
scoring.winCondition: Reach 100 or more cumulative points first, then apply game and line bonuses.

synthesis.shortDescription: Draw-discard duel where players build runs and sets, then score by deadwood difference with undercut and gin bonuses.
